title: 400 MCP Servers. 195 Answered.
caption:
I've installed MCP servers off a README list and never once checked whether they actually start.

Someone finally drew 400 at random from the official registry instead of picking the popular ones, and probed every single one. 195 answered. 150 never started at all — nearly three times the number blocked by a missing API key. Run the same probe against a hand-picked list of 24 servers and you get 66.7%. The curated lists aren't lying to you. They're just pre-filtered to the ones that work.

Worth saying: one author, not peer reviewed, and it only covers the npm/stdio slice of the registry. But the seed, the pipeline and every per-server result are published, which is more than most vendor benchmarks manage.

How many MCP servers are you running?

slides.title: Why 205 Didn't Run
items: 150 never started at all — the dominant failure.
53 were blocked by missing credentials. Barely a third as many.
2 packages were no longer available on npm.
One probe each, no retries — so 205 is a ceiling, not a floor.

slides.title: 58.8% Skip Safety Hints
slides.sub: 2,766 tools on the live servers. 58.8% carry no readOnlyHint or destructiveHint, so your agent can't tell what deletes.
